transformation.name: Transformation: What Stays the Same When Everything Changes
transformation.truth: Changing position, orientation or size changes possible passage. Ask which properties survive each operation and which body the resulting space admits.
transformation.qfep_connection: Transformations modify system states while preserving essential structure. In QFEP, transformations are the operations that change S while maintaining coherent identity. They are the grammar of change.
transformation.formula: p_new = M * p in homogeneous coordinates; translation adds a displacement, rotation changes orientation, scale multiplies dimensions.
transformation.demonstration: Collect, ride, turn, grow, approach and wait: seven halls connect a concrete operation to its spatial consequence.
transformation.description: Translation, rotation and scale taught through collection, crossings, constrained paths, rotated architecture and relative size. Bodily input and timed obstacles then test how these operations organise access.
learning_objectives: Distinguish collection from the translation, rotation and scale of an object.
Translate along x, y, z and combined directions without changing orientation.
Distinguish a destination from constraints on the journey to it.
Compare rotation axis, pivot and angle through crossings, arrays and repeated profiles.
Use uniform scale while holding the player and a reference doorway constant.
Distinguish reversible transformation from removal of geometry.
Compare body-driven openings with timed obstacles.
Name invariants precisely: translation and rotation preserve distances; uniform scale preserves angles and proportions, not lengths; non-uniform scale can change shape.
content: Trans_Pre: Observe the still cube before collecting it; three moving demonstrations remain. Add translation, rotation and scale, then climb to four finished pickups.
Trans_Introduction: Compare translation, scaling and rotation as crossings, without the head crab. Move the far bank while the plank keeps its motion: what makes the crossing possible?
Trans_Translation: Thirteen pickups sit on seven carrier routes through x, y and z. Two exit mechanisms share a destination but permit different journeys; the turning torus anticipates rotation.
Trans_Rotation: Compare a level Y bridge and upright X/Z rides, two body widths in rotated arrays, a tunnel and five carousel profiles. Which dimensions make space for this body?
Trans_Scale: Take the bottle: the room changes to four times its size in one update, then your body is relocated onto the table. Descend and compare the enlarged doorway with a fixed museum frame.
Trans_Body: Approach turns slats and shrinks blocks; contact cuts an open-topped trench in a low lattice. Step clear to see reversible openings return; the cut remains.
Trans_Pit: Three clear pusher lanes, turning gates and synchronised growers change access on level ground. Try the timed route or its bypass; ask which body has room and time to pass.

artifact_groups.rationale: Collect a still cube. Add rising, turning and swelling to its moving demonstrations, then walk a ramp to the completed pickups.
Cross by translation, scale and rotation; then slide the far bank while the plank keeps its original motion. Which part of the crossing did the background supply?
Seven journeys separate and combine x, y and z. At the exit, two hand-operated mechanisms share a destination but permit different paths.
Cross a level Y bridge; ride an upright end-platform forward around X or sideways around Z. Compare two body widths in the rotated arrays, then enter the tunnel and repeated cake profiles.
A four-metre room grows fourfold. The body keeps its size; descend the serving tower and compare a growing doorway with a fixed museum frame.
Approach turns slats, contact removes cells, proximity shrinks blocks. Two openings close behind you; one records your passage.
Position, orientation and size follow clocks. Read the moving obstacles and find when your body can pass.
